question.text: The frequency of echo will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi></math> if the train blowing a whistle of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>320</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> is moving with a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> towards a hill from which an echo is heard by the train driver. Velocity of sound in air is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>330</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
The hill will be a secondary source.

When the train moves towards the hill then, 

f1= frequency of the train w.r.t. the hill is f1=vv-vsf=330320×320=330 Hz

When the train driver hears an echo, then velocity of observer is v0=36×518=10 m s-1.

Now, f2= Frequency of the sound reflected by hill w.r.t. the car (echo)

f2=v+v0vf1=330+10330×330=340 Hz
